inputs: sequence: the pasted sequence as a string over the declared alphabet; normalized to bits (binary as-is; hex digits expand to 4 bits each, MSB first; decimal digits expand to 4-bit BCD, MSB first); n is the post-expansion bit length
alphabet: one of binary ([01]), hex ([0-9a-f]), or decimal digits ([0-9]); any other characters are rejected
sequence_label: optional caller-supplied label describing the source, for example 'audit sample batch 7', max 120 characters, carried into the receipt
name: Random Sequence Check
outputs: n: bit length after expansion; guard n >= 100 per NIST SP 800-22 rev1a §2.1.7 and §2.3.7
k: count of one-bits; V: observed run count

sequence_sha256: SHA-256 hash of the pasted sequence, carried in the receipt instead of the raw sequence. `sequence_sha256` is an integrity fingerprint, not a privacy guarantee; short or low-entropy sequences can be brute-forced from the hash.
monobit: integer comparison 62500*(2k-n)^2 >= 414681*n (fail when true); squared form of the §2.1 erfc test at alpha 0.01, no sqrt/erfc/log
runs: integer comparison 15625*n*(n*V - 2k(n-k))^2 >= 414681*k^2*(n-k)^2 (fail when true); evaluated only if monobit passes, otherwise "not_assessed" with reason "frequency prerequisite failed"
per_test_outcome: pass or fail per statistic against the documented integer thresholds, fail-to-reject framing only
what_it_computes: Takes a caller-pasted sequence of n bits over a declared alphabet (binary, hex, or decimal digits; n >= 100 per NIST SP 800-22 rev1a §2.1.7 and §2.3.7) and runs the §2.1 frequency (monobit) and §2.3 runs tests in pure integer arithmetic, with no sqrt, erfc, or log anywhere. With k ones and V observed runs, the NIST runs statistic z = |V - 2k(n-k)/n| / (2*sqrt(2n)*k(n-k)/n^2) rejects at alpha 0.01 when z >= x with erfc(x) = 0.01; x ≈ 1.8213864 gives C = x^2 = 414681/125000 = 3.317448, and squaring plus clearing denominators turns the test into the integer comparison 15625*n*(n*V - 2k(n-k))^2 >= 414681*k^2*(n-k)^2. The monobit test gets the same treatment: with S = 2k - n, erfc(|S|/sqrt(2n)) < 0.01 becomes the integer comparison 62500*(2k-n)^2 >= 414681*n. The runs test is evaluated only when monobit passes, per the §2.3.4 prerequisite; otherwise the receipt records runs as "not_assessed" with reason "frequency prerequisite failed". Each test reports pass or fail; the node can only fail to reject the sequence and never certifies randomness.
why_it_belongs: Sampling integrity matters in audits, testing, and compliance reviews, yet no AINumbers node verifies the statistical properties of a sequence. This fills that gap with a deterministic, fully re-verifiable check: pure math on caller-supplied input, no entropy sampled in-kernel, and an execution hash that recomputes exactly. Related nodes art-583 (beacon-seeded audit sampling) and art-471 (sampling frame builder) construct samples; this node verifies pasted sequences, a different function. The n >= 100 input-size guard follows NIST SP 800-22 rev1a §2.1.7 and §2.3.7: "It is recommended that each sequence to be tested consist of a minimum of 100 bits (i.e., n ≥ 100)."
